text: On the high-dimensional Kuramoto–Sivashinsky task, a degree-2 NVAR is more parameter-efficient than an ESN because its feature count stays small.
explanation: False. For KS with n=64, degree-2 NVAR already needs D ≈ 8384 features (and far more with higher degree/history), and the optimal kernels there are not low-degree polynomials. This is a regime where the ESN wins — e.g. Pathak et al. reach ~8 Lyapunov times with N=2400 neurons. NVAR's advantage is confined to LOW-dimensional, polynomial-structured systems.
